title: lvw-world-heavyweight
label: "Cowboy" James Donovan

won.source: "Supershow On The Strip I": won a 4-way, 60-minute Ironman match in sudden-death overtime, pinning Hans Nowak with the Oklahoma Stampede

lost.note: LVW's own records do not show how or when Donovan lost the title; "The Return" (16 March 2009) has a commentator state he "never lost the LVW Title in the ring," and "LVW The Story So Far" (10 March 2009) records the title changing hands repeatedly, including nine Gary Goldale reigns, before its own account resumes at a vacancy.

note: Untracked intervening reigns (Gary Goldale x9, others) are referenced only in the fed's own retrospective prose and are not separately recorded here.

title: lvw-world-heavyweight
label: J1D

won.source: "LVW High Stakes Battle Royal": won a 30-man battle royal for the vacant title, eliminating Olvir Arsvinnar last

note: LVW's own "4:18" (posted 4 August 2009) has J1D serve as special guest referee for a title-eliminator match rather than defend the belt himself, and the Showdown On The Strip line-up (10 August 2009) still bills him as champion; no later card survives.

title: lvw-las-vegas
label: El Gordo Grande

won.source: "Supershow On The Strip I": won the inaugural seven-man Final Table Match by putting Bill Bellmoth through a poker table covered in poker chips

note: Hard 8 (17 June 2006) shows the bracelet changing hands to Erik Mateo. LVW's own "4:18" has The Captain holding a bracelet, which is the separate Strip Championship (won 1 June 2009).

lost.source: "Hard 8": lost the Las Vegas Championship to Erik Mateo (clothesline, pinfall) in the booker's short-form write-up

title: lvw-strip
label: The Captain

won.source: "Snake Eyes": beat Olvir Arsvinnar for the inaugural Strip Championship after Aaron Roddick broke a baseball bat over Olvir's head

note: By LVW's own "4:18" the Captain holds the bracelet he won from Olvir; no later card shows it changing hands.

title: lvw-las-vegas
label: Erik Mateo

won.source: "Hard 8": beat El Gordo Grande with a clothesline for the Las Vegas Championship in the short-form write-up

note: The roleplay of 5 July 2006 calls him the new Las Vegas Champion; in August 2009 he says he was the one who left LVW holding the Las Vegas title. No card shows the end of the reign.
